newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares end off as profit-taking starts.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares end off as profit-taking starts.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange fell back from record highs as a long-awaited bout of profit-taking kicked in, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index fell 1.60 percent to 9,515.75, as 27 stocks fell, 14 rose and six closed flat.
Brokers said profit-taking would likely continue for the rest of the week as stock valuations adjust to a prolonged rally which has taken prices to successive highs in recent sessions.
A total of 72.3 million shares worth 8.731 billion bolivars ($17.9 million) changed hands, down on recent sessions.
Among leading stocks, bellwether Electricidad de Caracas slipped 24.25 bolivars to 801.00 bolivars for its first loss since being awarded a 75 percent rate hike June 26.

Telephone company CANTV fell 20.00 bolivars to 3,100.00 bolivars, while cement company Vencemos class 1 stock fell 29.00 bolivars to 995.00 bolivars and class 2 stock fell 25.00 bolivars to 925.00 bolivars.
